title: Documents carry a branch on every operation, but branching and merging operations are planned rather than implemented
content:
Every operation is keyed by branch as well as document and scope, and `main` is the default — typically the published version. Custom branches are described as drafts, experiments or parallel versions, and operations are **isolated per branch**.

What does not exist yet is the machinery to use them: the architecture states plainly that **branching and merging operations are planned but not yet implemented.** So the storage layer will hold operations on any branch name a caller supplies, and nothing will create a branch from another, diff two branches, or merge one into another.

For anyone designing on top of this: a draft/published workflow can be *stored* today by writing to a second branch name, but the promotion step has to be implemented in application code (re-submitting the actions against `main`), and there is no reactor-level guarantee about how the two histories relate.
